$comment: The REVIEWED expectations for the Sampler build (review finding F002): written at the guideline phase, changed only with the operator. scripts/tests/test_font.py compares the built fonts against THIS file, never against font.json, so a font.json edit that lowers a floor or drops an axis or a character goes red here.
titles: A Field Guide to Wet Stone
$comment_tables: tables pins the font-table decisions build.py makes by default (review: fontbakery findings of 2026-11-16). prep_hex is the smart-dropout program (PUSHW 0x01FF, SCANCTRL, PUSHB 4, SCANTYPE) that pairs with the gasp above; code_page_range1 is OS/2 ulCodePageRange1 (bit 0, Latin 1); mac_names false means the name table has no Macintosh (platform 1) records. names.fs_type is the embedding permission, 0 here because the example is built from MIT example parameters. vertical_metrics (per group) is the reviewed line height: hhea and OS/2 typo carry these numbers with a line gap of 0, and win covers every glyph.
$comment_qa: accepted_qa_findings: every FontBakery FAIL or ERROR the project accepts, with the reason (scripts/fontbakery-gate.py). case_mapping: the generator draws the lowercase ì î ò ù û ā š and no uppercase counterpart for them; adding the capitals is a generator change (references/generator.md, adding glyphs), not a build setting.

accepted_qa_findings.reason: the generator's glyph set has the lowercase ì î ò ù û ā š and not Ì Î Ò Ù Û Ā Š (seven pairs, listed in FontBakery's message); the fixture's titles need none of them, and a capital is a new skeleton, which is a generator change

the roman and the italic file carry no `ital` axis in STAT (FontBakery wants ital 0, elidable and linked to 1, in the roman and ital 1 in the italic, so a font picker can pair the two files); the build does not write it because the roman's STAT would then depend on whether an italic group exists, and browsers do not read STAT; a later change to build.py
the example's italic is a one-axis group (wght) beside a two-axis roman (wght and opsz), which is the shape it exists to exercise; FontBakery expects every file of a family to carry the same axes
the same fact as family_axis_ranges: the italic file has no opsz axis (FontBakery: lacks a 'opsz' variation axis)

each group measures its own glyph extent (the roman 957, the italic 956 units), and the two files are built one at a time, so build.py cannot give both the family's maximum; typo_metrics would equalise hhea and typo but not the measured win metrics; a later change to build.py
